newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber trends lower in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber trends lower in quiet trade.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market was subdued by midsession on Tuesday with sellers on the hunt for scarce buyers, dealers said.
"I heard there were several sellers in the market this morning, but I have not seen a lot of buyers and they seem to be waiting for the afternoon session," a dealer said.
"We're just waiting for something to drop from heaven. I think most of the buyers will wait for the Kobe market to close before making any decision," another dealer said.
The Songkran Buddhist holiday in Thailand, the world's biggest producer of natural rubber, weighed on market sentiment.
"We're seeing very little of the Thais in the market. I don't think they will back immediately tomorrow so it will take some time for the holiday mood to disperse," one dealer said.
Market activity may slowly wind down ahead of the Eid Al-Adha Moslem holiday on Friday, which will shut down markets in Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia, dealers said.
At around 0430 GMT, June RSS3 was indicated at 113.75 U.S. cents a kg from 114.75 cents. June RSS1 was indicated at 164.25 Singapore cents (US$1.14) a kg from 164.00 cents.
June TSR20 was indicated at 155.50 Singapore cents (US$1.08) a kg from 156.25 cents. - (US$1-S$1.44) Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
